title: MabletonLink critical service directory
geography: Residents of the City of Mableton, Cobb County, Georgia
scope: Curated essential and commonly needed services from city, county, school district, state, utilities, and agency-designated platforms. Not an exhaustive inventory of all government services or utility providers.

verification_definitions.public_page_reviewed: Public landing page or public instructions reviewed through web research. Does not verify account-only features or transactions.
verification_definitions.official_link_verified: Destination and purpose confirmed through an official agency or provider page; destination content or workflow could not be fully inspected.

action_url_note: Optional action URLs were confirmed through official pages. No login, application, report, purchase, or payment was completed.
homepage_note: The 12 featured entries are editorial starting suggestions, not measured resident demand. Keep emergency access separate and persistent; offer provider-specific utilities based on resident choice.
maintenance_notes: Check municipal boundaries before routing city services; a postal city name is not proof of jurisdiction.
Keep city SSD, county property-tax, municipal court, and permit/license payments separate.
Private trash haulers determine routes and schedules; do not invent a citywide pickup calendar.
Select utilities by actual provider; this directory is not a complete address-to-utility service-territory map.
CobbLinc Go requires confirmation before launch: its official page describes a two-year pilot from October 29, 2024.
Recheck police routing as Mableton transitions; current city FAQ says Cobb County coverage continues through May 31, 2027 and describes a planned city launch on June 1, 2027.
School maps and inspection cutoffs may become stale; link to the current operational page instead of copying dates or times.
Review official-link-only entries in a normal browser before launch, especially CTLS Parent's redirect behavior.
Check links monthly and before launch; review payment, emergency, election, transport, and jurisdiction changes more frequently.
